key_insight: Detonation-spraying settings strongly control whether self-fluxing Ni–Cr–Fe–B–Si–C coatings become dense and wear-resistant or smoother with lower friction but higher wear.
engineering_relevance: The study provides practical parameter guidance for restoring and strengthening machine parts by balancing coating density, hardness, friction, and wear resistance.
method: Adjusted working-gas ratio (O/C = 1.026–1.856) and inter-shot delay (0–1 s).
Compared coating morphology, roughness, hardness, friction, and wear response.
evidence_signal: The best wear resistance was achieved at O/C = 1.856 with 1 s inter-shot delay, lowering specific wear rate to 0.000189 mm3/(N·m), while the lowest friction occurred at 48% barrel filling and O/C = 1.026.
watch_item: Optimizing for low friction can conflict with wear resistance, and higher filling levels may introduce residual-stress-driven microcracks.
paper_title: Development of a Method for Producing Self-Fluxing Nickel-Based Coatings by Detonation Spraying
